topic: CSA Trusted AI Safety Expert (TAISE) certification exam preparation - the Cloud Security Alliance's award-winning AI safety and security credential covering the full AI lifecycle: generative AI architecture, ethics and explainability, AI threat taxonomy, model governance and risk, AI security and safety, cloud and data security for AI, and privacy
exam_format: Proctored exam of 60 multiple-choice questions, 120 minutes, passing score 80%, with 2 exam attempts included (valid for 2 years). TAISE is a TRAINING-PLUS-EXAM bundle - there is no exam-only option, so candidates must complete the official CSA training to sit the proctored exam. No formal prerequisites, though basic familiarity with AI, cloud, and security concepts is recommended. Confirm current pricing on the CSA site (the figure here is approximate for the training+exam bundle).
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: Security, governance, risk, and compliance professionals, AI/ML practitioners, and architects who need to secure and safely govern AI systems. Fits naturally alongside AI-governance credentials this catalog already covers (IAPP AIGP, ISACA AAIA/AAIR/AAISM, Microsoft SC-500, CompTIA SecAI+). No deep coding required. NOTE: because TAISE officially requires CSA's own training to sit the exam, this course is positioned as independent companion prep and conceptual mastery, not a replacement for the mandatory CSA training.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: AI and Generative AI Foundations
domains.notes: Covers TAISE modules 1-3: introduction to AI and machine learning; generative AI architecture and design (LLMs, transformers, embeddings, RAG, agents); and generative AI use cases and applications across the enterprise. Core vocabulary and mental models the rest of the exam builds on.

domains.name: AI Ethics, Transparency, and Explainability
domains.notes: TAISE module 4: ethics, transparency, and explainability in AI - fairness and bias, interpretability/explainability techniques, accountability, human oversight, and responsible-AI principles applied to real deployments.

domains.name: AI Model Lifecycle and Threat Taxonomy
domains.notes: TAISE module 5: the AI model lifecycle (data, training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, retirement) and the AI threat taxonomy - adversarial attacks, data poisoning, model inversion/extraction, prompt injection, jailbreaks, supply-chain and model risks mapped across the lifecycle.

domains.name: AI Governance, Risk Management, and Compliance
domains.notes: TAISE module 6: model governance, risk management, and compliance - AI risk frameworks (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001), the EU AI Act and emerging regulation, CSA's AI Controls Matrix (AICM), policies, audits, and mapping controls to AI risks. Strong overlap with the catalog's governance courses - cross-sell angle.

domains.name: AI Security and Safety; Cloud and AI Security
domains.notes: TAISE modules 7-8: foundations of AI security and safety (securing models, pipelines, prompts, and agents; guardrails, red-teaming, safety evaluation) and cloud and AI security (securing AI workloads on cloud, identity and access, isolation, secure MLOps, shared-responsibility for managed AI services).

domains.name: Data Security and Privacy; Continuous Learning and Adaptation
domains.notes: TAISE modules 9-10: data security and privacy in AI systems (data protection, privacy-enhancing techniques, PII handling, data minimization, training-data governance) and continuous learning and adaptation (monitoring, drift, incident response, keeping AI safety practices current as threats and regulation evolve).

extra_guidance: CSA TAISE (Trusted AI Safety Expert) is a 2026 SC-Award-winning AI safety/security credential and a strong fit for this catalog's existing AI-governance cluster (IAPP AIGP, ISACA AAIA/AAIR/AAISM, Microsoft SC-500, CompTIA SecAI+) - cross-sell those in the funnel. Marketing angle: 'master AI safety and security with complete prep for CSA's Trusted AI Safety Expert'. IMPORTANT positioning/accuracy note: TAISE is officially a TRAINING-PLUS-EXAM bundle with no exam-only path, so the course must be positioned honestly as independent companion/concept prep and NOT claim to replace CSA's mandatory official training - say this plainly in chapter 1 and the description. Exam facts to use: 60 multiple-choice questions, 120 minutes, 80% to pass, 2 attempts over 2 years. The 10-module official curriculum is: (1) Introduction to AI, (2) Generative AI Architecture and Design, (3) Generative AI Use Cases and Applications, (4) Ethics, Transparency, and Explainability in AI, (5) AI Model Lifecycle and Threat Taxonomy, (6) Model Governance, Risk Management, and Compliance, (7) Introduction to AI Security and Safety, (8) Cloud and AI Security, (9) Data Security and Privacy in AI Systems, (10) Continuous Learning and Adaptation - the six domains above consolidate these ten modules; keep all ten module topics covered. ACCURACY note: the percentages above are editorial (CSA presents roughly ten modules of comparable weight, not official percentages) - present the module/topic names as official and the weights as approximate. Ground heavily in CSA's own materials conceptually: the AI Controls Matrix (AICM), CSA AI guidance, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, OWASP LLM Top 10, and MITRE ATLAS for the threat-taxonomy content. Practice questions should be scenario-based (choose the right control/framework/mitigation for a described AI risk) with plausible distractors. Labs here are tabletop/architecture exercises (threat-model an LLM app, map controls with AICM, build an AI risk register, design guardrails) rather than console walkthroughs. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 120-minute / 60-question / 80%-pass time-management strategy. Keep content vendor-neutral (CSA is vendor-neutral); still scan the practice bank per the pipeline compliance rules.
